brief: Morgan Stanley's 2027-28 US outlook: resilient growth, reluctant disinflation. AI-related hyperscaler capex ($1.6tn in 2027, $1.8tn in 2028) anchors growth, but because imported servers and chips are netted out of GDP, the AI buildout does not overheat the domestic economy; growth holds at 2.5% in 2027 and 2.6% in 2028. Consumer spending leans on wealth effects from asset gains tied to the AI rally among upper-income households, even as real income growth stays soft, so consumption moderates to 2.0% in 2027 before rebounding to 2.3% in 2028. Inflation falls reluctantly: tariff payback and softer airfares pull core PCE toward 2.6% in 2027, but energy pass-through and healthcare costs keep disinflation slow, with PCE finishing modestly above target through 2028. This leads the Fed to hike 25bp in December and March to 4.25-4.5%, consistent with a neutral rate MS now estimates near 150bp, before cutting 75bp in 2028. Fiscal impulse fades, deficits hold near 6% of GDP, and the debt ceiling binds by February 2027. Four alternative scenarios bracket the baseline on demand, productivity, oil/rates, and an AI spending pullback.
